coverage_notes: All registered anchors on PDF pp.3-4, composition Table I and method/temperature text p.2, and paper title/material preparation p.1 were visually inspected. Render font warnings did not obstruct the readable evidence.
shared_qualifications: C11: V vs SCE x 1000 = mV vs SCE. Terminal scan rates are 54 mV/h /3600 = 0.015 mV/s for the commercial/high-purity alloys, and 60 mV/h /3600 = 0.0166667 mV/s (CRA rounded 0.017) for the 18Cr-2Mo series. Initial sweeps are ten times faster; those stages are not conflated.

Table I NA means not analyzed but assumed within the series. In CRA 355/356, populated Cr/Mo/C and other inferred series values are not independent measured source analyses. The nominal series and measured Ni identify those heats.

Source Table I and Table IV identify the high-Ti alloy as 1.86 wt.% Ti; CRA 359 Ti is 1.88, while its original Comments names 1.86. This composition conflict is retained; the exact table row and other conditions support identity.

Table IV >0.80 V entries are strict scan bounds without a definite threshold before transpassivity, not measured pitting at 0.80 V. The distinct instantaneous-potential-jump outcome obs_015 (+0.40 V) is not equated to that scan bound.

Fig.4 obs_013 is an individual representative run, while CRA 353 is a source-reported average. Its contribution to that average is not explicitly identified, so the connection remains candidate-only. obs_014 transient repassivating-pit initiation is a separate result definition.
